mac_setup_notes: Hardware: Apple M5 Max with 64 GB unified memory, 2 TB SSD, macOS high-power mode on AC (methodology.md "The machine"). Apple's spec page lists 64 GB only for the M5 Max with a 40-core GPU, which has 614 GB/s memory bandwidth (https://www.apple.com/macbook-pro/specs/). So for a model fully in VRAM, this laptop's 896 GB/s is about 1.46x the Mac's bandwidth (estimate). Engine: Ollama 0.32.13 and 0.33.0, called through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint http://localhost:11434/v1, not /api/chat (setup.md). The engine version changed outcomes: gemma4:12b went from 5/5 to 1/5 on one cell between 0.32.13 and 0.33.0 with the same digest. Supported models were re-verified on 0.33.0 at their most marginal cell (methodology.md). qwen3.8 now needs Ollama 0.32.12 or later (registry config "requires":"0.32.12"). Dates: methodology.md says 22-23 August 2026, but measured-profiles.json says qwen3.8:27b was chosen on 2026-10-09, so the roster was measured over a longer period than that. Digests were not recorded. Several tags have been rebuilt since: qwen3.5 tags show "1 month ago", qwen3.6:35b "2 weeks ago", and qwen3.8:latest is now 18 GB against 19 GB in the README. Pass bar: six surfaces (Investigate, Optimize, Assess, Operate, Analyze, Plan), each run five consecutive times against the embedded SQLite sample, scored on verdict `answered` and not on whether the SQL is correct. The prompts are small. That is far below OpenCode's 64k and the 3,648-token first request. Turn limit: 90 s per model turn is the shipped default. qwen3.5:9b, qwen3.6:27b and qwen3.6:35b carry 150 s (turnTimeoutMs 150000). Median and slowest figures cover whole agent runs, not tok/s. Sampling: the harness default is temperature 0, top_p 1, which overrides the Ollama tag params (qwen3 tags ship 0.6/0.95, qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 ship 1.0/0.95). Exceptions: qwen3:8b runs query-optimization at 0.8/0.9, and a separate qwen3.8:27b profile uses temperature 0.3. Thinking: left at the model or Ollama default (on for the qwen3, qwen3.5, qwen3.6 and qwen3.8 families) unless the profile sets suppressPlanReasoning (qwen3.5:4b, qwen3.6:27b, qwen3.6:35b) or suppressAgentReasoning (qwen3.6:27b, qwen3.6:35b). The reasoning effort sent to qwen3.8 is not recorded. Context: only qwen3.6:35b records it, OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768, because unbounded it asked for more memory than 64 GB. The other runs presumably used Ollama's VRAM-based default (4k under 24 GiB, 32k for 24-48 GiB, 256k at 48 GiB or more, https://docs.ollama.com/context-length), which is not stated. Other per-model knobs: qwen3:14b planStatementRetries 1; qwen3.5:9b retryEmptyTurn; retryUnreadStop on qwen3-coder:30b, qwen3.5:27b and qwen3.6:35b. Thermal: a long unbroken sweep lost 18 of 270 cells to heat, and every lost cell was re-measured on a rested machine. The methodology itself says the pass/fail result transfers and the seconds are a best-case lower bound for a 16 GB laptop. Tool parsing: the Ollama qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 tags use Ollama's own renderer and parser ("renderer":"qwen3.5" or "qwen3.8", "parser":"qwen3.5"), and qwen3-coder:30b uses "qwen3-coder". The tool-call reliability shown therefore belongs to Ollama's parser path, not to llama.cpp's Qwen3-Coder XML parser (open issue #30118). Sources: $HOME/projects/libredb/libredb-studio/docs/llms/methodology.md, setup.md, model-tuning.md, qwen/*.md, and $HOME/projects/libredb/libredb-studio/src/lib/agent/model-tuning/measured-profiles.json (read only).

models.fit_detail: Weights 2.33 GiB. KV is 36 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 x 2 x 2 B = 144 KiB/token f16, so 9.0 GiB at 64k. Total about 12-12.5 GiB with about 1 GiB of graph and CUDA context, under 15.47 GiB. 128k needs q8_0 KV (about 4.8 GiB at 64k, 9.6 GiB at 128k). Host RAM need is small, a few GiB (estimate). Needs OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536, because the default here would be 4k.
models.best_runtime_here: Ollama with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 (f16 KV fits), or 131072 with OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 and OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0. This is the exact runtime and parser path the harness validated. llama.cpp works too but adds nothing for a model this small.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: Faster (estimate). It fits fully, so decode is bandwidth-bound at 896 vs 614 GB/s, about 1.46x, and prefill on the RTX 5080 is far stronger than the Mac GPU. Rough decode: about 180-230 tok/s here (scaled from TechFuelHQ qwen2.5:7b at 177 tok/s on a desktop 5080, times about 0.93 for the laptop). Run durations are dominated by thinking tokens, so expect them to shrink by roughly 1.3-2x, not to change in kind.
models.opencode_suitability: Tools yes, thinking always on (Thinking-2507 has no off switch), 256K native context. The harness shows very reliable tool calls: 30/30 at temperature 0 with no settings. But it is a 4B model: KB discovery calls small models weak for serious coding, and it is not a primary OpenCode model.
models.reason: It is the cheapest harness-verified tool caller that fits fully at 64-128k, so it is a good Ollama smoke test and a fast sub-agent. It is not a replacement for the KB's ranked picks on coding quality.

models.fit_detail: Weights 17.28 GiB exceed 15.47 GiB. KV 48 x 4 x 128 x 2 x 2 B = 96 KiB/token: 6.0 GiB f16 or about 3.2 GiB q8_0 at 64k. Ollama's whole-layer split at 64k f16 would keep only about half the layers on the GPU. llama.cpp keeps attention on the GPU (about 1 GiB of non-expert weights) and puts about 19-21 blocks of experts (about 0.34 GiB each, about 6.5-7 GiB) in RAM at 64k with q8_0 KV. Host RAM need is about 9-11 GiB, so a container cap of 12-14g (estimate).
models.best_runtime_here: llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407 with -ngl all --n-cpu-moe 20 (tune 19-22), -c 65536 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja (Qwen3-Coder parser). Per the KB, it beats Ollama's layer split for a spilling MoE. Ollama with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 is the fallback that matches the harness parser path.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: Slower or similar (estimate). The Mac holds all of it in 614 GB/s unified memory. Here the offloaded experts are read from DDR5 at a 102.4 GB/s peak. Estimated decode is about 50-80 tok/s on llama.cpp (TechFuelHQ measured 51.6-61.9 tok/s on desktop Ollama), against a likely 80-110 tok/s on the Mac. Prefill on Ollama offload was 1525-2369 tok/s on the desktop 5080. Its run durations (11 s median) should stay short because it does not think.
models.opencode_suitability: Tools yes, thinking none, 256K native context. The harness gives the strongest tool-call reliability evidence in the lane: 30/30 at defaults, no malformed arguments, no narrating. Independent coding-agent scores are weak (TB2.1 13.5), so it suits a fast tool-calling worker more than a planner.
models.reason: The KB excluded it on coding benchmarks. The user's harness shows it is the most reliable and fastest tool caller in the lane, and a 3B-active MoE runs acceptably with --n-cpu-moe.

models.kb_status: top 10 rank 2: llama.cpp ggml-org Q4_K_M with --n-cpu-moe 21, 128k f16 KV, --reasoning off. Ollama qwen3.6:35b-a3b with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 is the fallback (docs/model-selection.md, llamacpp/models.md).
models.fit_detail: Weights 20.23 GiB plus a 0.84 GiB projector. KV 10 x 2 x 256 x 2 x 2 B = 20 KiB/token: 1.25 GiB at 64k, 2.5 GiB at 128k. The Ollama layer split at 64k keeps roughly 24 of 40 layers on the GPU. llama.cpp --n-cpu-moe 21 keeps attention and KV on the GPU and puts about 8.9 GiB of experts in RAM. The KB estimates 13.5-14.1 GiB on the GPU and sets a 20g container cap (estimate).
models.best_runtime_here: llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407 with the KB recipe (-ngl all --n-cpu-moe 21 -c 131072 --jinja --reasoning off). Ollama 'qwen3.6:35b' with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 is the fallback and matches the harness parser.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: Slower (estimate). The Mac holds all 22 GB at 614 GB/s. Here about 9 GiB of experts are read from DDR5. The KB's inferred decode is 40-90 tok/s against likely 80-120 on the Mac. With thinking suppressed, turns are short, so the 13 s median should become something like 15-30 s, still well inside 90 s.
models.opencode_suitability: Tools, thinking toggle, 256K native context with the cheapest KV in the lane. The harness shows reliable tool calls only with thinking off on agent turns. With thinking on it is not unreliable, it is too slow to finish a turn. Only 32k context was exercised.
models.reason: It is the KB's rank 2. The harness confirms its tool reliability and validates the KB's choice to start the server with thinking off.

models.underlying_model: Qwen3.8-27B, dense hybrid attention (16 of 64 full attention), MTP, vision (HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B). Today qwen3.8:latest, qwen3.8:27b and qwen3.8:27b-q4_K_M share config sha256:492b2922d38e and model blob sha256:f5f1dd8920d4.

models.kb_status: top 10 rank 1, as the llama.cpp unsloth UD-Q3_K_XL (12.24 GiB) fully on the GPU at 64k with q8_0 KV and reasoning effort medium. The KB calls the Ollama qwen3.8:27b (18 GB) 'Not recommended' because it spills (llamacpp/models.md, docs/model-selection.md).
models.fit_detail: The Ollama Q4_K_M weights (15.66 GiB) plus a 0.87 GiB projector plus 4 GiB f16 KV at 64k come to about 21-22 GiB, so about 6 GiB of dense layers land in DDR5. The KB's UD-Q3_K_XL path fits fully: about 11.7 GiB on the GPU, 2.1 GiB q8_0 KV at 64k, about 15.2 GiB total (estimate).
models.best_runtime_here: llama.cpp with the KB rank-1 recipe (UD-Q3_K_XL, -c 65536 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja --reasoning-effort medium). Not Ollama.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: Slower on Ollama Q4_K_M: a dense spill gives about 11-13 tok/s against about 25-35 on the Mac, and the Mac's 2:50 assess run would break the 90 s turn limit here. Faster on llama.cpp 3-bit in VRAM: the KB infers 40-45 tok/s. But that is a different quant from the one the harness passed (estimate).
models.opencode_suitability: Tools, thinking toggle with effort xhigh, medium or low, 256K context. The harness shows reliable tool calls at Q4_K_M with thinking left on. The KB's medium effort, the 3-bit quant and the llama.cpp Qwen3-Coder parser (issue #30118) are all untested by the harness.
models.reason: It is the KB's rank 1. The harness adds first-hand agent-loop reliability for the model family, but not for the KB's quant, runtime or effort setting. The KB's verdict against Ollama on this laptop stands.

kb_implications: Add the libredb-studio harness to docs/sources.md and docs/community-benchmarks.md as a first-hand evidence class: '(measured on the M5 Max, libredb-studio)', Ollama 0.32.13/0.33.0 through /v1, temperature 0, 90 s turns (150 s for some models), small SQLite prompts. State that pass/fail transfers and that the durations do not, because they are whole-run times on 614 GB/s unified memory.

Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B (excluded on SWE-bench Verified 31.8 and TB2.1 13.5) is the most reliable and fastest tool caller in the harness: 30/30 at defaults, 11 s median, zero argument errors. Move it from 'Excluded' to an honorable mention as a fast non-thinking tool-calling worker or sub-agent, with a llama.cpp recipe: -ngl all --n-cpu-moe about 20, -c 65536 with q8_0 KV, because its KV is 96 KiB/token, 6 GiB f16 at 64k. Keep it out of the top 10 on coding-quality grounds.

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (rank 2): the harness confirms tool reliability only with thinking off on agent turns. With thinking on, optimize timed out at 200-350 s on six readings. This confirms the KB's '--reasoning off' server default and argues for keeping the OpenCode default variant at no thinking. Note that the harness ran it only at OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768.

Qwen3.8-27B (rank 1): the harness shows 30/30 for the Ollama Q4_K_M build with thinking at default. That supports the model, but not the KB's UD-Q3_K_XL quant, the llama.cpp Qwen3-Coder parser path (#30118) or medium effort. Add 'repeat the six libredb surfaces against the llama.cpp UD-Q3_K_XL server' to 'What to measure first'.

Correct llamacpp/models.md line 86: the claim that qwen3.8:27b's 'digest differs from 27b-q4_K_M' is now false. Live registry manifests for qwen3.8:latest, :27b and :27b-q4_K_M all use config sha256:492b2922d38e and model blob sha256:f5f1dd8920d4 (16,810,714,464 B), with a 931,146,016 B projector, and require Ollama 0.32.12.

Qwen3.5-9B (honorable mention, vLLM NVFP4 path): the harness gives 30/30 for the Ollama Q4_K_M with a 150 s turn limit and an empty-turn retry. Add an Ollama or llama.cpp path that fits fully at 128k (5.24 GiB of weights plus 4 GiB of KV, estimate) as simpler than building the vLLM NVFP4. It is a cheap first Ollama measurement on this laptop.

Confirm the existing exclusions of Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.6-27B: the harness passes them but slowly (78 s and 82 s medians), and Qwen3.6-27B needs both reasoning suppressions and 150 s turns. The Ollama Q4_K_M builds spill here, so the timings would collapse.

Small Qwen3 (qwen3:8b, qwen3:14b) pass the harness but have a 40,960-token native context, below OpenCode's 64k. Record them as excluded for OpenCode with that reason, not as unevaluated. qwen3:4b is today the Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 build (256K, same manifest as qwen3:4b-thinking-2507-q4_K_M) and fits fully at 64-128k. List it as a harness-verified smoke-test or sub-agent model.

The Ollama Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 tags use Ollama's own 'qwen3.5' renderer and parser. The harness reliability therefore belongs to that parser and does not prove the llama.cpp Qwen3-Coder XML parser that the KB recipes rely on. Where a model fits fully in VRAM (qwen3.5:9b, qwen3:4b), Ollama is a legitimate runtime choice here and reuses the evidence directly.

The harness does not cover these KB picks: K2 Horizon MoVA 36B A4B, K2 Horizon 7B, Qwen3-Coder-Next, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt, Groot-19B-A3B and DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B. gpt-oss:20b and gemma4:26b are covered in other lanes. Rank 1 is covered only at a different quant.

Add the M5 Max bandwidth fact (614 GB/s for the 64 GB, 40-core-GPU configuration, https://www.apple.com/macbook-pro/specs/) to community-benchmarks.md as the scaling basis. A model fully in VRAM here should decode about 1.46x faster than on the user's Mac, and a model that spills to DDR5-6400 should decode slower.

The qwen3:14b profile's 'measured' string still says '5/6 modes locked, 29/30', while the page and README count it as 30/30. The re-run that closed plan after planStatementRetries 1 is not recorded in the string.

The Ollama context length during runs is recorded only for qwen3.6:35b (32768). For the others it was presumably Ollama's VRAM-based default on a 64 GB Mac, which is not stated. No run exercised 64k-scale prompts like OpenCode's.
The reasoning effort sent to qwen3.8 (template default xhigh or Ollama's own) is not recorded, so how the harness pass relates to the KB's medium-effort setting is unknown.

No Qwen model has been run on this laptop. Every fit, KV and speed figure here is arithmetic (estimate) from the registry blob sizes and HF config.json. Ollama is not pulled, so whether Ollama clamps num_ctx to the 40,960 native context for qwen3:8b and qwen3:14b is unverified.
The non-expert versus expert split for Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B (about 1 GiB versus about 16.3 GiB, hence --n-cpu-moe about 20 at 64k) is my estimate from config.json, not read from a GGUF header.
The M5 Max prefill speed is not known from an official source, so the 'faster here' claims for in-VRAM models rest on bandwidth plus the general compute gap and are not measured.

The harness checks that a run read, presented and cited data, not whether the SQL was right, and it uses one small SQLite database. It is strong evidence of tool-loop reliability but not of coding quality for OpenCode.
